summary: Identity-proxy claim rewrite removes delegated 'groups' claim, preventing temporary access to oncall runbook tool
description:
Issue summary: Temporary delegated access links (just-in-time approvals) issued by the support portal generate valid tokens, but users are unable to assume the expected runbook roles. We observe successful SSO flows (200 / SAML assertion accepted) but RBAC evaluation on the oncall-runbook service fails because the 'groups' claim is missing or rewritten as 'grp_ns_v1'.

Impact: Engineers cannot escalate into the oncall runbook UI using short-lived delegated tokens. This blocks emergency playbook execution and oncall handoffs for ~10% of approval flows in us-west during business hours, causing delayed incident response.

Observed behavior: Tokens include a groups-like attribute but under a different key (e.g., 'grp_ns_v1', 'groups_v2'), introduced after a recent identity-proxy rollout that normalizes SCIM attributes into a namespaced schema. The runbook RBAC expects claim key 'groups' (string array) and performs exact-key checks. When the claim key mismatches, the user is treated as unauthenticated-for-role and sees a 403 on /runbook/assume-role.

Notes: This appears intermittent: some customers' accounts still get the original 'groups' claim (older SCIM entries), while others (recently provisioned/updated) get namespaced claims. SCIM profiles for affected users include a mapping rule 'append_namespace=true' in the synchronizer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use internal support portal to create a delegated access link for user 'svc:jdoe' to assume 'runbook-admin' for 30 minutes.
2) Click the approval link and complete SSO (Okta/SAML) from us-west environment.
3) Observe the token returned by the identity-proxy; inspect JWT claims (groups vs grp_ns_v1).
4) Attempt to call POST /runbook/assume-role with Authorization: Bearer <token> and observe 403 when 'groups' claim is absent.
5) Compare with same flow for a user whose SCIM profile was not touched by the new mapping; that token contains 'groups' and the assume-role call succeeds.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:12:03Z identity-proxy INFO accepted SAML assertion for user jdoe (okta-id: 00u123)
2026-03-10T15:12:03Z oncall-runbook WARN rbac: claim 'groups' not found; eval failed for token sub=00u123; returning 403
2026-03-10T15:12:18Z scim-synchronizer INFO patch user 00u123 mapping: add namespace 'ns_v1' (append_namespace=true)
hypothesis: The recent identity-proxy/SCIM synchronizer change began namespacing SCIM group attributes. Runbook RBAC uses an exact claim key ('groups') instead of a flexible lookup for namespaced claims, causing authorization to fail for users whose SCIM entries were touched by the new mapping.
mitigation: Short-term: revert identity-proxy rollout for the namespace rewrite in us-west to prevent further regressions (rollback queued).
Workaround: support can manually issue a token with an explicit 'groups' claim by running the internal token-rewrite script (support-only) — documented in the incident channel.
Medium-term: add claim normalization adapter in oncall-runbook to accept namespaced variants (grp_ns_v1, groups_v2) and update RBAC evaluation to search a claim-mapping list.
resolution_notes: Engineering has validated the claim mismatch hypothesis and opened a fix branch to add a claim-normalizer upstream of RBAC evaluation. Rollback of the identity-proxy namespacing was deployed to us-west on 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC which reduced new occurrences to zero; affected users were fixed by reissuing tokens. Pending tasks: PR review and canary rollout of claim-normalizer; update Confluence runbook for future SCIM mapping changes.
